approach: Use the window height and speed to find the launch speed, then check whether 3 s falls before or after the ball reaches its highest point.

steps.text: The ball moves upward past the window at 10 ms⁻¹ at a height of 15 m. Use this to find the launch speed u from the ground.
Find the time taken to reach the highest point.
Since 3 s is later than 2 s, the ball has already passed its highest point and is coming down. Find its velocity at t = 3 s using v = u − gt, keeping the upward direction positive.
A negative value with upward taken as positive means the ball is moving downward at 10 ms⁻¹.

common_mistakes.text: Computing v = 20 − 10(3) = −10 correctly but not checking that the ball has already passed the top, and reading the 10 ms⁻¹ as still moving upward.
Using the window speed 10 ms⁻¹ directly as the launch speed u instead of solving for u from the window height and speed, giving v = 10 − 10(3) = −20 ms⁻¹.
